lessons.title: Bir kamusal öneriyi karşı itiraza rağmen gerekçelendir
lessons.objective: Bir topluluk önerisini kaynak ve ölçütle savun, en güçlü itirazı doğru aktardıktan sonra önerini sınırla.
lessons.situation: Bir mahalle ikinci el eşya günü planlıyor. Sergileyiciler yeterli alan, sakinler açık kaldırımlar istiyor.
lessons.bridge: Admittedly ile itirazı kabul et. Even so ile gerekçeli karşılık ver. İtirazı ciddiye alacak bir tasarım değişikliği öner.

models.phrase: Admittedly, an extra stall could narrow the path.
models.explanation: Admittedly sınırlı bir itirazı açıkça tanır. Could olasılık bırakır.

models.phrase: Even so, a marked walkway would let us test the plan safely.
models.explanation: Even so itirazı koruyup yanıta geçer. Would önerilen düzenlemenin beklenen etkisini verir.

concepts.label: Taviz ve gerekçe bağlayıcıları
concepts.incorrect: Admittedly the path is narrow. Therefore, there is room for more stalls.
concepts.correct: Admittedly, the path is narrow. Even so, we can test one smaller stall.
concepts.explanation: Taviz karşıt bir yanıta açılır; therefore neden-sonuç ister.
guided: İtirazı kabul et: ___, the venue is expensive. (Admittedly / Therefore)
İtiraza rağmen çözüm: The room is small. ___, a short session could work. (Even so / As a result)
transfer: There are fewer seats. ___, we should test timed entry. (Even so / In the meantime) İtirazı koru.
___, the northern route is longer. (Admittedly / Similarly)
delayed: Bookings rose. ___, the board kept the fee. (As a result / Admittedly)
The proposal has risks. ___, a smaller trial is worth considering. (Even so / For example)

concepts.label: İtiraz ile koşullu çözümü eşleştir
concepts.incorrect: “Wheelchairs cannot pass.” “We could print better posters.”
concepts.correct: “Wheelchairs cannot pass.” “We could keep a wider lane clear.”
guided: “Residents cannot sleep.” Uygun cevap: end earlier / hire a pianist.
“Some people never see online notices.” Cevap: paper notice / longer link.
transfer: “Queues block the pavement.” Cevap: stagger arrivals / add a banner.
“Visitors may trip in the dark.” Cevap: light the route / redraw the price list.
delayed: “One volunteer cannot count entries and answer calls.” Cevap: split the tasks / change the sign.
“The cheapest tickets sell out before people leave work.” Cevap: reserve an evening batch / shorten the poster.

writing.prompt: Bir gençlik etkinliği için 115–155 sözcüklük savunu yaz. İtiraz akşam gürültüsü olsun. Teklifi yeniden sınırla ve hangi gözlemden sonra uzatma isteyeceğini söyle.
writing.sample: I support a short outdoor music trial because young people have few places to perform and rehearsals inside the centre are already crowded. Admittedly, somebody who lives next to the gate could be disturbed even by one performance. I would therefore limit the trial to two early evenings and keep the speakers away from the houses. The centre could give neighbours a number to call while the event is running, when staff can still turn the sound down. A comment made the next morning would also be recorded. If both evenings end on time and the nearest households report no repeated disturbance, the committee could consider another trial. If the same problem is reported twice, it should move the performances indoors.
writing.revision: İtirazı yanıtlamayan önerileri çıkar. Kimin, neyi, ne zaman gözleyeceğini ekle.
criteria: Karşı görüş sahibi ve gerçek kaygısı açık.
Koşullu öneri yeni bilgi gelirse değişebilir.

input.text:
Neighbourhood proposal. The swap day would let residents exchange children’s clothes and furniture. The organisers want eight stalls near the bus stop because it has shelter. A residents’ note asks for a clear passage along the pavement. When prams and wheelchairs meet at the corner, the kerb already creates a bottleneck. The organisers suggest keeping the first two stalls away from the corner and limiting larger items to a room inside the library.

Access team response. A daytime trial period could show whether a marked lane stays clear at busy times. Volunteers should count blockages rather than record only total visitor numbers. Before the second event, check the layout with residents who use the route daily. Moving a table is reversible; promising eight stalls to traders before that check is harder to undo.
reading: Which feedback fits the access team’s concern?
Count blocked passages, then review the layout
Count all visitors without noting access
Add two stalls at the corner
input.transcript: Chair: The market could bring useful services closer to residents. Jo: Admittedly, more stalls could make the corner harder to cross. Lena: Could we put the bulky things inside the library? Jo: That addresses space, but should we also mark a clear lane? Chair: Yes, and before promising a second Saturday, ask someone to count how often the lane is blocked. Lena: If the route stays clear, we can invite volunteers back. If it does not, we must move the corner stalls.
input.preparation: İtirazın iki cevabını ve karar için ölçümü dinle.
detail: What happens if the lane is blocked?
Başarısız denemenin yeni eylemi köşe tezgâhlarını taşımak.

retry.text: A local library will test deliveries at 7 a.m. Residents worry about noise. The team will use the rear yard only and record complaints before making the time permanent.
reading: Use the rear yard and record complaints
Erken teslimatı arka avluda sınırlandırır ve şikâyeti ölçer.
retry.transcript: Two neighbours support a book exchange but worry about boxes on the stairs. We could put one shelf by the side door. If it blocks the exit, we will move it inside.
retry.preparation: What problem and exit condition does the speaker name?

lessons.readingPurpose: Öneri, karşı görüş, koşullu uyarlama ve yeniden karar için dört madde yaz.
lessons.readingUse: Bir gürültü veya erişim sorununa hedefli değişiklik öner.
lessons.listeningUse: Karşı görüşü önce muhatabın kabul edeceği biçimde geri söyle.
lessons.speaking: Bir gece yürüyüşü öner. Partner güvenlik itirazı getirsin. Ölçülebilir bir değişiklik ve uzatma şartı öner.
